Subject: Sovereignty acceptance checklist & temporary cross-region hop during DR

Marcus —

Thanks for the intro last week. As we proceed with the procurement and security review I need a concise description of how Redwood will honor an EU residency commitment for Helix Health data, and under what narrowly-defined conditions transient cross-region processing may occur (e.g., disaster recovery, 72-hour warmup windows, telemetry aggregation). Specifically, the InfoSec and legal teams want: 

- A short acceptance checklist we can include with the DPA addendum (what Redwood will guarantee vs. temporary exceptions).
- Clear maximum duration for any temporary cross-border hops and the authorization flow (who approves, audit trail).
- Confirmation of KMS boundary behavior when keys are customer-managed and whether key unwrap can happen outside EU during a failover.
- Subprocessor roster for the EU region and whether any analytics or telemetry processors are US-based.
- Sample runbook describing the operational trigger and TTL for a transient hop (I prefer a single-page summary).

We are trying to avoid broad language like "may process in other regions" without constraints. Can you send the checklist + a short runbook and point to any supporting evidence (audit logs, KMS architecture diagram)? Tobias from procurement is copied for contract sequencing.

Thanks,
Julia Kaplan
CISO, Helix Health

(attachment: requirements-helix-v2.pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
To: Julia Kaplan <julia.kaplan@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Sovereignty acceptance checklist & temporary cross-region hop during DR

Hi Julia —

Thanks for the clear ask and for looping Tobias in. High level answer up front: Redwood can provide an EU-residency commitment with a tightly-scoped, auditable transient-hop policy for DR and short-lived operational windows. I attached a one-page checklist and a runbook summary to this message. Key points: 

- Residency commitment: Customer data for pinned routes (you can map API keys or routes to region) will be stored and processed in EU-hosted instances by default. Full support for customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) is available; key unwrap operations are tied to HSMs located in the EU when BYOK is enabled and the key policy restricts unwrap to EU audit nodes.

- Transient hop policy: Allowed only for the following conditions: (1) declared DR activation, (2) verified capacity emergency (documented) or (3) short operational maintenance where EU infrastructure is unreachable. Max duration: 72 hours without executive escalation; any extension requires written approval from your security contact and Redwood's Security Lead. All transient hops will be recorded with start/end timestamps, affected routes, and invoked fallback model versions.

- Audit & authorization: Every transient hop must be approved by on-call SRE + Security (two-person authorization) and is logged in our immutable audit stream with a signed timestamp. We provide an extractable CSV and a Drive folder with the logs for third-party review on request.

- Subprocessors: The attached roster lists infra and telemetry subprocessors by region. Analytics/telemetry aggregation for platform health uses a privately contracted vendor based in Ireland. No US telemetry processors for EU-pinned routes except for anonymized, aggregated billing metrics (safe-harbored) if you opt in — we can disable that for Helix by default.

I'll summarize the attachments here: residency-acceptance-checklist.xlsx — one-page commitments and required DPA clauses; temp-hop-runbook.md — operational steps, authorization matrix, and rollback criteria; subprocessor-roster.pdf — current EU roster + contact emails.

Next steps: 1) Please confirm whether Helix wants BYOK enforced for the pinned routes; 2) if you want the 72-hour cap hardened to 24 or 48 hours we can propose contract language; 3) we can prepare a DPA addendum and DocuSign package once you confirm the above.

Attestations and evidence referenced: audit log extract (Drive link in email footer) and a short KMS architecture diagram (available on request).

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com
+1 415 555 0142

(attachments: residency-acceptance-checklist.xlsx; temp-hop-runbook.md; subprocessor-roster.pdf)

---
Notes: The runbook includes the authorization flow (SRE on-call + Security), automated revert policy at 60 minutes if service degradation detected, and a post-mortem template to be delivered within 5 business days after any transient hop.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Fwd: Sovereignty acceptance checklist & temporary cross-region hop during DR — operational clarifications

Kimberly / Marcus — forwarding Julia's ask and the checklist I just reviewed. A couple of operational clarifications we should confirm before we send the evidence package to Helix: 

1) BYOK behavior: With customer-managed keys we currently run key unwrap only on EU HSM cluster if the key policy has the EU restriction flag. We need legal to approve the proposed wording "unwrap restricted to EU HSM when BYOK enabled" to avoid ambiguity.

2) Telemetry processors: The roster shows an analytics vendor in Dublin (OK) plus a backup aggregator in the US used for non-identifiable billing telemetry. We should mark billing telemetry as "opt-in" for EU customers by default and document the data minimization approach (tokenized IDs only).

3) TTL cap: Ops prefers 72h as a reasonable fallback; Security prefers 24h. Marcus — can you confirm whether the automated rollback triggers and the 60-minute revert window are implementable for EU-pinned routes without risking split-brain? If not, suggest language we can commit to in the DPA (e.g., automatic metrics-based reversion but with human approval for extension).

I recommend we add a single paragraph to the checklist describing the approval flow and the exec escalation path (who signs extension beyond TTL).

Marissa
Director, Customer Trust Ops
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com
